correctness.rationale: White-side first-force obstruction gives at most two uncolored vertices in each part. A two-white side requires a missing matched endpoint; if both sides have two whites, the nonempty matched index sets must differ. Direct case reduction completes forcing. Counting pairs with matched endpoints and exclusion of equal index sets gives coefficient C=A2*B2-t(a-t)(b-t)-binom(t,2); every initial white has at least b-3 or a-3 black neighbours, hence domination. An independent graph bitmask full-subset enumeration for 15 profiles corroborated. The all-parameter proof is combinatorial rather than empirical.
